utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. If the witness could be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. If you would please sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If I could remind you that you took an affirmation when you commenced your evidence to tell the truth and that remains in force. Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Rodic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Valjalo. I will continue my cross-examination now.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to ask you the following: I have been cautioned by the interpreters, since we both speak the same language and understand each other, to pause between question and answer. So if you could please wait for my question to be interpreted first before providing your answer so that both could be correctly interpreted into English. Thank you. In view of the fact that you have lived in Dubrovnik for a very long time, you are probably familiar with your town. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You probably know a great many people in Dubrovnik, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know a great many people, yes. Perhaps not by name, but certainly many people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anyone who was a member of the army or the National Guard Corps or the Territorial Defence or perhaps a police officer, any aspect of the Croatian armed forces, the HSP at the time defending the town?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: HSP, no, not really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So no one at all from the National Guard Corps, from Territorial Defence, from the local police, from the HOS, none of those members?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I can remember now. Not by name anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anyone given any medals, decorations in Dubrovnik on account of their participation in the defence of the town?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was probably the case, but I can't remember any of the specific names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not a single name?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Truth to tell, I really can't remember any particular individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If, for example, you had participated in the homeland war, the defence of Dubrovnik, would you be ashamed to say so publicly?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you contribute in any way to the town's defence?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think by the very fact that I didn't leave the town while others were attacking it, I did give a contribution, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your family, however, fled Dubrovnik, and you saw your family while you were away for treatment, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. We only reunited once I arrived in Rijeka for treatment. The day before I entered the hospital to be treated, I went to see them at Rabac, which is where they were staying. I think it was a Sunday. I spent a night there, and the next day I was off to the KBC Rijeka hospital to receive treatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me why immediately upon leaving the hospital you hurried back to Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because Dubrovnik is my home. Dubrovnik is my town. I had no reason to stay away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Couldn't you have remained with your family?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my family, too, was due back. They could have stayed on where they were, but their desire was to go back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, you returned to Dubrovnik on your own without your family, at least not right away.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We went back together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On examination-in-chief, you said that you returned to Dubrovnik but that your family stayed back and that they only came back later.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The family did not come to Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't go straight back to Dubrovnik or, rather, right now I can't remember precisely, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a reason why you had to return immediately?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no particular reason or obligation. I just wanted to go back to work, that was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you officially an invalid of war?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever observe the Croatian army firing from Dubrovnik itself?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never observed anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear or see any shells being fired from Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard or saw anything like that. I was in the Old Town, and there was no way for me to see anything like that happening from within the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me how long you've known Mr. Sikic?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hadn't known him before he became the president of the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long was that for? When he was appointed president?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember what year it was. I can't remember. I can't say with any degree of precision, because I simply don't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long had you known him for prior to the 1st of October, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had not known him before then. I never met him prior to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was your first meeting?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he came to the municipal assembly in Dubrovnik. Was that October, November, December, or earlier on in 1991?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can't you even tell us roughly when this was, because you said that you had gone to see that man, that you had worked as his driver.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ever since he arrived and took up his duty, I worked as his driver, and that's how long I've known him for. That was perhaps September 1991, or August possibly. As soon as he took up his duties in Dubrovnik, but when that was precisely, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a driver by the name of Stjepan?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I do know him, but the name doesn't really ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was Nojko Marinovic's driver. Does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I used to know Nojko Marinovic's driver, but I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Kreso Madic who was Djuro Korda's driver?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Maybe I actually know the man, it's just that I don't know the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Zeljko Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zeljko Pavlovic who was with the TO? Is that the man you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were Zeljko Pavlovic's whereabouts during the war in 1991?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think at first he was with the Territorial Defence, but where he was later, I really can't say. I didn't exactly keep track. It wasn't my job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where he was stationed, where his HQ were?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was where the military recruitment office used to be, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where Villa Rasica is?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's at Lapad. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that where the National Guard Corps was stationed at the time?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go there at the time, but yes, I think so. There was something there. I didn't see anything myself because I didn't go, but I think it was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the exact whereabouts of the aquarium?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's in the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you specify its location? Can you relate it to another building inside the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: St. John's Fort, I believe, is the nearest thing, the nearest point of reference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that where the TO headquarters were?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never went to the TO headquarters, and I don't know its whereabouts. I know that refugees had been put up at the aquarium and there was a shelter there. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if there was any such thing as a TO headquarters stationed there?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where Villa Palma is?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is the police building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was there?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to the outbreak of the conflict, was the police also there or were they in a different location?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the police were always there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that even prior to the outbreak of war in the Dubrovnik area the police station was at Villa Palma? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, To the best of my knowledge, I think Villa Palma was always the police building. I was not aware of anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any artillery units stationed there, positioned there?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any artillery. I saw police officers. Actually, there was a lorry there that tried to break through and drive on to Mokosica. There was a lorry. I'm not sure if that was the one, but there was one like that. I really don't know what the name was. The lorry was used to transport food, people. You couldn't pass through Rijeka Dubrovacka because there were sniper positions up on Golubov Kamen and they were targeting people down in Rijeka Dubrovacka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was about artillery and you're telling me about a lorry that was bringing bread to Mokosica.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd never seen any artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe this lorry for me, the one that you saw transporting bread to Mokosica?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a special lorry. They put some sort of an armour on it that was apparently bulletproof so they would not be hit. They used that lorry to drive through. I think even the armour -- the body of the car was reinforced and apparently bulletproof. I'm not sure what the type the vehicle was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that vehicle personally?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In passing, yes. I'd see it sometimes outside Villa Palma.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any weapons mounted on that lorry?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no weapons so ever, not that I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know this lorry was used to transport bread to Mokosica?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard people talk about that, that the lorry was used for transporting bread or medicine. Somehow the lorry would be able to get through, but that's only what I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the lorry would usually be parked outside the police building. Who drove it to get the food through?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I should expect one of the police officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So why would a lorry be stationed outside the police headquarters if it was only used to transport food to a different place?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the police, I presume, were not in charge of the bakeries in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably the bakeries were not part of their remit, I expect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any Croatian army artillery pieces in Dubrovnik at all?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not a single item, never in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have the usher's assistance for a moment. Can you please put this on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the town of Dubrovnik itself, did you ever see a lorry like this?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw it in Dubrovnik itself, nothing like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A lorry or a vehicle with a three-barrel gun mounted. You'd never even heard of its existence or seen it anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear about something like this moving about town?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have that back, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any such thing as civilian protection in Dubrovnik that was actually up and running?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what their task was?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say. I never sought to ask anybody. I had my own job to worry about, so I really didn't keep track of anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know at all what the civilian protection would have been in charge of, what their job would have been?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know really. I could only speculate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in charge of attending the wounded in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hospital, I guess. I suppose some of the civilian protection people were putting out fires, picking up the wounded. I suppose this was also done by the civilian protection. They were clearing the streets, but this was also done by other people on a voluntary basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In early October 1991, did you see any ships, any navy ships? If so, where exactly did you see those and what exactly did you observe?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In early October?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What exactly did you see? Can you specify, please?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 1st of October, which is when I heard sounds of shelling, I was on duty at the municipality then and you could hear shells exploding from the east. I came out on the building's roof, and I saw that the area, the road leading out of the town, the main road, was being target just above Zlatni Potok. I saw a warship that was targeting the area directly. Later on, I went home. The house was full of my relatives who had fled the Konavle area. I told them what was happening and hoped that this wouldn't come to anything. There were small children there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw this on the 1st of October when you were on duty in the municipality? That's when you could see this?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Later when I went back to work, I'm not sure where it was that I went. Maybe I just happened to be at Boninovo. I saw two planes targeting Srdj. Probably the -- they were trying to hit the repeater at the top of the hill so there was no telecommunication. Telephone lines were cut and the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for how long did your shift last on the 1st of October when you watched this? How long was your shift?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 10.00, I think, in the evening until, I think -- I can't be very precise about the time in the morning, but I think it was around half past seven or 8.00 in the morning on the following day, that is the 1st.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain, then, as you were in the night-shift and on duty in the municipality from, let's say, 10.00 p.m. until 8.00 a.m., did you change shifts on the following day? Were you off? How did this go?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We changed shifts, but we were afraid. The war had already Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. started, and no one was able to sleep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anyone else on duty besides you? Did you have a chance to get some rest?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did get some rest. All I had to do was answer the phone if it rang.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else was on duty at the municipality in the same way as you?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who it was before me, but we would switch. Somebody was always there by the phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your task while you were on duty?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: To answer the phone and take notes and report on the following morning when the president or somebody arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see gunships of the navy near Lokrum?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they shooting at anything?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were. They fired shots I think at Lokrum, Bosanka, although I did my military service, I don't know much about projectiles, but I knew what gunships sounded like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you recognised the shots fired by gunships. You could tell them by sound.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because they sound different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do they sound different?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when a gun fires, it goes Duum, but when a gun ship fires, the sound is a bit different: Duum, duum, duum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're sure you never heard sounds from Dubrovnik that would sound like weapons being fired?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent almost all my time in the Old Town at the municipal assembly or at home in Prijeko. On several occasions we went to the shelter in the Centar school or in the defence building in Dubrovnik where there was some concrete slabs. I didn't move much outside the Old Town. And while I was in the Old Town, I did not hear shots being fired from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when I say from the town of Dubrovnik, I'm not referring only to the Old Town but to the broader Dubrovnik area.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear anything in the Dubrovnik area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you drive around at all in that period?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I stayed in one place more often than I drove around because of the shelling. We couldn't drive around. It was dark. When we tried to drive at night they would shoot, probably from Zarkovica. There was a gun there that rotated. And below Srdj there were snipers probably. They had fragmentation bullets. They had rockets illuminating the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me in your estimation how many alarms were sounded in Dubrovnik in that three-month period? How many alerts were there?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but there were lots. There were warnings very often. And once it went on for five days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the alert, where were you? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: During alerts, we were all supposed to be somewhere safe. So I was either at the municipal building while my family was there. I would join them because of the children, to reassure them and my wife. The children are still traumatised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where would you go?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to the Centar school most often and sometimes in the Institute for Restoration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when your family left, where would you go then when there was an alert?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: With my late father-in-law who worked in the restoration institute, I would be with him, or I would go to the Centar school, or I would remain at work. I wasn't there on my own, and I felt safer there. Sometimes I would spend the night there -- or, rather, I would spend the night in my flat in Prijeko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In November, was there any shelling of Srdj? In November.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You aren't sure?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In November? Yes. Yes. Yes, yes. In November. Now I recall. I think for four or five consecutive days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can you tell me who held positions at Srdj?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Croatian army in the Imperijal fortress and the Yugoslav army held positions below that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether the Croatian army fired back from Srdj?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you. So many shells and bullets were fired up there I can't tell you who fired them. I think that soldiers could not leave their shelters because of the thousands of shells that were falling, but I didn't see the people up there who were shooting. I only saw the shells falling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were the shells falling from?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were coming from all sides, from the sea, from the land.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All falling on Srdj?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I think that was when the cross on Srdj was hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that the Croatian army did not fire at all from Srdj?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I'm saying. I didn't see that happen. I know that on the 6th of December, they responded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how they got their supplies? Did they have ammunition?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did get supplies. They went on foot dodging the shells from the main road on the other side, and shells were fired on them, on the food supplies being brought in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On Sustjepan were there any ZNG position?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know this?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go to Sustjepan, but I know it was the first line of defence, and a friend of mine is today a complete invalid because his spine was injured at Sustjepan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of weapons did they have at Sustjepan?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that because I didn't see them. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the Croatian army also held positions below the main road.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, according to what people said, they were billeted in houses there, in family houses. They were protecting the town from there, otherwise everything would have been surrounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is the main road from the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main road is right there overlooking the Old Town, maybe some 600 or 700 metres away, or a kilometre. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that how far it is to the main road from the city walls?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the crow flies, I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me how far below the main road were the Croatian army positions? Were they stationed in peoples' houses?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them, I just heard about it. The houses were right by the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I can see on the map, there are houses between the Old City walls and the main road. Were they at the main road or closer to the walls or in the middle? What did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you, because I didn't see them. I heard that they were in houses right next to the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you saw JNA positions; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you saw these positions at Zarkovica, at Bosanka.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above Bosanka, up there. About 2 or 300 metres below Srdj. There was a dugout there. And when I looked through my binoculars, I could see soldiers and the dugout there. And you could see the same at Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you looked at them through binoculars, from where were you able to see and observe all this?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But where exactly in the Old Town? From which position? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Porporela, from the municipal assembly, and also from the Stradun, from the Excelsior Hotel, the Argentina Hotel. I saw them from there as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you issued with those binoculars?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were my personal property.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they military style binoculars?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, civilian ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you always carry binoculars with you to work?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I kept them in my car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Besides being by the phone, did you have to observe as well? Was observation part of your duty?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, on what occasions did you observe this all through your field glasses then?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I had nothing else to do. Then I would take out my field glasses and have a look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you report to anyone about what you saw?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because anyone could see that. You could even see that without field glasses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me which cafe is located near the municipal building?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Gradska Kavana, the city cafe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's not a cafe.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was referring to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you draw a distinction between a building such as the Gradska Kavana and a cafe?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there cafes in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, which cafe or how many cafes are there near the municipal building?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Near the municipal building, well, on the Stradun there are cafes all over the place, two, three of them. Some of them are patisseries. There is one called Trubadur.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you leave the municipality you had a cafe close by. Which was the closest one? Where did you have coffee when you left the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the Stradun. That's where most people went to have coffee, the snack bar on the Stradun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the closest cafe to the municipal building? I'd like to know which one is the closest.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The terrace in front of the municipality, the Gradska Kavana was the nearest place to have coffee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is that from the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's in the same building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Gradska Kavana?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's at the entrance to the municipality. The Gradska Kavana terrace is there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On examination-in-chief on Friday, you stated that on the 6th of December, you were at the municipal assembly, and you said that an attack from the east had begun early that morning. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, from the east. That's where the sounds of shelling came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that the night between the 5th and the 6th of December you spent at the municipal assembly manning the duty phone. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why, then, when my learned friend and colleague asked you for the second time the same thing you answered that you were back at home with your brother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When exactly are you saying?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On examination-in-chief, you said, in answer to the same question, you said that on the 6th of December you were at the municipal assembly building. You said that an attack had begun from the east early in the morning and that the night between the 5th and the 6th of December you stayed at the municipal assembly building as the official who was on duty by the phone. That's what you said on examination-in-chief when you were asked this for the first time. And my learned friend and colleague interrupted your testimony, and you added later that you were at home with your brother-in-law. A minute ago I asked you whether it was true that you were at the municipality -- municipal building and you said this was correct. Can you tell me how such a discrepancy can arise in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about the 6th of December; right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the question. I assume, since you are an invalid of war, that you were wounded in the line of duty, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the line of duty, yes, because there was the Crisis Staff. So I was the president's driver, and that's why I was granted the status of an invalid of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could any civilian who was injured in Dubrovnik be granted the same status as you or does it have to be something special?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not everyone could be granted that, but I think the Crisis Staff had a statute, and whoever was a member of the Crisis Staff was granted - and was wounded - was granted the status of an invalid of war and all the remaining people were granted the status of civilian casualties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This means that you were mobilised at the time, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't mobilised, but I was supposed to be there at work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We agreed that back in 1991 you were at an age where you were still a potential military conscript, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told me that before 1991, you were a part of the reserve forces and you had taken part in military drills as such.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you are wounded and you are awarded the status of an invalid of war, which cannot be granted to any other civilians who were wounded in Dubrovnik, well, then, this must be in some sort of connection with a military duty that you had, because the name itself says it, an invalid of war; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not wear any uniform, any military uniform. I did not receive anything in writing. I was simply told that it was my work assignment to -- to go and work there. There was no one to replace me because there was just one other driver at the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, you did have, after all, an official capacity that places you in connection that made it possible for you to be given the status of an invalid of war and receive compensation.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I told you, after all, that I was the driver of the president of the Crisis Staff, so that's why I was granted the status of an invalid of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is no such regulation in place, in fact. Now that you're a driver for the county prefect, that's no -- that is not linked with any military status, is it?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you been a driver for the bishop and had he been wounded in the line of duty, would you also have been granted the status of an invalid of war?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I probably wouldn't have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did hold an official post with the municipality which entitled you to be granted the status of an invalid of war.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My only duty was as a driver for the municipal assembly. I was the driver of the president of the Executive Board, and now I'm an official driver for the Dubrovnik Neretva county for the county prefect. So these are the only official posts that I hold.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it not true that you did part of your military service as a driver?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a soldier or civilian at that time?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: A soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, a driver, too, can be a military officers?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yet you have the status of an invalid of war.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The night between the 5th and 6th of December, you were on duty by the phone at the municipal assembly building; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not December. It's not December I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the 5th and the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was only on duty for a single night, and that was on the 1st of October. That's what I'm telling you. That's when the attack on Dubrovnik began. I don't think I stated anything like that. I was only on duty for one night at the municipal assembly building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, unfortunately that's exactly what you told me five minutes ago, and it's the same thing you said on examination-in-chief. However, as soon as you stated that on Friday during the examination-in-chief, the counsel for Prosecution interrupted you; isn't that correct? Is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Frankly, I don't remember. 6th of December, I had already been wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or at least that's what you say.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about the 6th of December; right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 6th of December. And you say that you were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not something I'm saying. That is the truth. Well, I think you can still tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Valjalo, I'm not challenging the fact that you were wounded. Now, as to whether it was on the 6th of December and where exactly you were wounded, I think that's something I'm trying to challenge.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's nothing to challenge there. I have all the documents. Everything I stated was true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After your family had left, did you spend more time with your father-in-law at home or at work?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At work. My father-in-law spent more time in the shelters with his own friends, and his sister also lives nearby, so he would often go and see her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you can remember, how many times did you stay with your father-in-law in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember specifically how many times. We did see a lot of each other, but usually we only saw each other very briefly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did you spend the night in the same flat as your father-in-law throughout that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember, but more often than not it was in the shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the firing began, which specific shelter would your father-in-law go to?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually he would go to the Centar school building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any other shelter that he went to?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was another one that I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is very specific. Was there any other shelter that he went to throughout the period?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the institute, the restoration institute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The restoration institute. Is that near the municipal building?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which shelters did you go to together with your father-in-law, if you did?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. The Centar school building, I assume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the general alert started, where were you when you first went to the school shelter?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were on the ground floor, sometimes on the first floor, in a classroom, some classroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. What I mean is something else. Where was it from that you would head for the shelter that was in the school building in the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the time this was when my family was still around, and I would go with them. And my late father was also still around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When in November your family left Dubrovnik, where would you go, to which shelter?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: After my family left, I would spend all of my days at the municipal assembly which I also used as the shelter at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That was the best shelter you could find, at work. Near the municipal assembly building, there was another shelter, the restoration institute. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you worked as a driver for Zeljko Sikic, did you ever go to Prevlaka with him?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, once specifically. I think it was before the attack began, the attack on Konavle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that in September 1991?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was there at Prevlaka at the time?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't actually enter Prevlaka. We drove as far as Prevlaka. There was a cabin there, and then Mr. Sikic left. He was supposed to meet someone, I'm not sure who, but I stayed there and waited for him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any JNA barracks on Prevlaka?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's just that I didn't see them. You couldn't go any further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, did the army complain about the Croatian police deploying themselves along the border?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those other people were at a meeting. I'm not sure who Mr. Sikic was seeing, but there was a military officer there. I'm not sure about the rank. So he asked me why the Croatian police had deployed themselves and the ZNG along the borders. They were not exactly polite.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The rank of that military officer doesn't matter, but it was a JNA officer, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was this JNA office doing there? How exactly did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Sikic was off to the meeting, and I parked my car there, and there were two other gentlemen there and one of them was just sitting there and talking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Sikic meeting members of the JNA at the time?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I assume so. It was some civilians that he was meeting or some JNA people. I don't know, because I didn't see who he was meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zeljko Sikic was the TO commander for the Dubrovnik area, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was the president of the Executive Board. That is all he was. And later he became the president of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Last time I asked you and you said you had given a statement in Dubrovnik on the 20th of May, 2000, to the investigator Dirk Hooijkaas, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will read sentence -- the second sentence in passage two of your statement now: "During this time I was a chauffeur for Zeljko Sikic the head of the Territorial Defence for the Dubrovnik area. " The balance of the passage is identical to the rest of your testimony a while ago when you answered my questions about you being at Prevlaka about the JNA making complaints about the Croatian police being deployed, whereas here you seem quite decided that you worked as a driver for Zeljko Sikic who was the commander of the Territorial Defence for the Dubrovnik area. Isn't that what it seems?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't notice that, but I suppose this was a mistranslation. I said that this was not the Territorial Defence but, rather, the Crisis Staff later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea when the work commander of the Territorial Defence for the Dubrovnik area is being translated and president of the Executive Board of the Dubrovnik municipality, these two bear no resemblance to each other, do they, in any of the languages?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Commander of the Territorial Defence on the one hand and president of the Executive Board of the municipality on the other, in the Croatian language, do these two sound alike at all? Could you perhaps confuse the two? Do they strike you as similar?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know if they sound alike or not. I don't think they do but it's not for me to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the word "gun" and the word "pen"? Do these two words sound alike?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about these two -- let's try these two, the commander of the TO and President of the Executive Board of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not the same thing, as far as I can tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree with you there.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is that this was mistranslated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you say it was mistranslated but these are two completely different things. They couldn't be farther apart. Did anyone perhaps advise you to say that this was a mistranslation?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no one advised me. I noticed this myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came here and read the statement again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this statement it says that you read it before signing it in the year 2000. You read the statement then, and you did not correct it.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I didn't notice the mistake at the time. I certainly didn't, otherwise I would have corrected it then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since this can hardly be a mistranslation, a misinterpretation because we agreed just awhile ago that the two terms do not resemble each other, is this right?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And especially not according to their meaning. The duties of the commander of the Territorial Defence is something quite different from the duties of the President of the Executive Board of the municipal assembly. Isn't that right? Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the Executive Board is one thing, and the head of the national defence is something else, in my view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with respect to the kind of work they do, isn't there a big difference between the two?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is. I think there is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that you were wounded on the Stradun, you said that you got to the city cafe, the Gradska Kavana, wounded as you were. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you first aid?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My friends and the waiters working there. And in the municipal assembly, they called an ambulance. But unfortunately, there was such heavy shelling that the ambulance couldn't come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they sent two members of the Territorial Defence to help you from the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody from the municipal assembly sent them. They volunteered to brave the shells in order to collect the dead and wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they told that someone had been wounded?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They just happened to be on the Stradun when the late Pavle Urban, the photographer, was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the things you are talking about now? You were wounded. You were in the cafe lying down. Did you see him being killed?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that case, we will not talk about it.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. But I'm just trying to say that when the van arrived on the Stradun, the waiters heard it coming. They thought it might be an ambulance. They saw that it wasn't, and then they said to those gentlemen, "There's someone here who's seriously wounded. Would you please take him? This one is dead anyway." That's what I heard them say. So they picked me up and took me to the hospital in the Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher assist me, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you orient yourself on this map and indicate the house and the Old Town where you lived.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My house?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. On this map if possible.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise, but can you mark this place and write the number one next to it?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now also mark with the number 2 the school, the Centar school in the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. I think Miha Pracata Street is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark with the number 3 the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if this will be a hundred per cent precise, but I'll do my best. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would the usher please put the numbers 1, 2, and 3 next to the marks made by the witness. THE USHER: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you mark on this map the Institute for the Protection of Monuments?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This will be number 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just mark the place and the usher will put the number 4 there. That's the Institute for the Protection of Monuments.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's this building here. One or the other of these. I'm not a hundred per cent sure, but it is in this location. Oh, you said for the protection of monuments. I marked the Institute for the Reconstruction of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that where the shelter was?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's the institute I mean.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is it, but I'm not sure which of these two buildings it is, but it's around here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That will be number 4, then. Can you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you make the Adriatic Highway, the main road on this map? Can you mark it with number 5.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell on this map where the Croatian army positions were below the main road, as you described it? Can you draw a line there and mark it with number 6.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't go up there. I didn't see them myself. I just heard that they were up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can you mark where it was that you heard that they were?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In the Prosecution's submission it has absolutely no probative value if the witness is being asked to mark on a map things which he knew and saw about with the numbers 1 to 5 or 6 and then on the map to mark things which he only heard about which is purely speculative. The two should not be mixed. In my submission he should not be allowed to mark on the map something which he was only told about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is the evidentiary value for the Chamber, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with respect to my learned friend's objection, I can do without number 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We'll leave it that way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before my learned friend goes on, it appears, Your Honours, that then he's -- the witness is marking it in red. This is just an administrative point. It may not copy. It might be better if they marked it in blue or black.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We won't change the matter at the moment. If it becomes a problem, the -- we will learn for future marking, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you put a number 7 next to the place where you were allegedly wounded.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not allegedly, it's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would suggest it be number 6, Mr. Rodic. We haven't a 6.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 6, then, marks the place on the Stradun where you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately. I can't be completely precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 3 is the location of the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can't orient myself on a map all that well but, yes, that's where it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief, you said that from the place you were wounded, you entered the City Cafe.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have we marked the City Cafe on this map?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we haven't, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show us where it is?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I just can't be precise. But it's right -- the entrance is right next to the entrance to the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that would be number 3. The City Cafe is in fact in the same building?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's a terrace in front and on the left-hand side is the entrance to the City Cafe. There are two entrances, in fact; one by the fountain and the other one. There's an entrance here at the side, and then this is where the fountain is, and then the other entrance. So one of the entrances to the City Cafe would be here, and the other one is where the terrace is, and there are two entrances there, one for the City Cafe, one to the municipal assembly, and then there's a third one leading to the theatre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So number 3 marks both municipal assembly building and the position of the City Cafe, because they're right next to each other.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The City Cafe is on the ground floor and has a terrace overlooking the sea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I tender this map with the markings, and I ask that it be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be received, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D23.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, when you were wounded, why didn't you go to the municipal assembly but to the City Cafe?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I could barely summon the strength to get that far, and that was the nearest place to go. I saw someone going to the City Cafe in front of me, and it was the nearest door. I staggered in and said, "I've been wounded," and my friends the waiters sprang to my assistance. And that was the only reason, it was closer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement to the investigator, you said, "It took me a great effort to reach the cafe where I was given first aid. The waiters at the cafe called the ambulance, but the ambulance could not come because of the shelling. A little later, some people from the National Guard Corps or the Territorial Defence took me to the hospital." Is it true what is stated here in your 2000 statement?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, except it should say the Gradska Kavana, the town cafe. And those two people who came to take me away were wearing camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We also ascertained a while ago that you draw a distinction between Gradska Kavana, town cafe, and just any cafe. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a distinction but I said Gradska Kavana, the town cafe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this again a mistranslation perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a typo perhaps. I'm not sure what sort of an error it was. In my statement I said Gradska Kavana, the town cafe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We might have a mistranslation there because there is a very small difference between town cafe and just cafe.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may well be the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But command of the TO and President of the Executive Board of the municipal assembly, well, that's quite a distinction, isn't it? We did agree on that didn't we?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, except I never said that Mr. Zeljko Sikic was the commander of the TO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Prosecution objects to the repetition of this particular line of questioning, and there is one other -- the witness has already answered it in some detail before. There was an objection I should have made earlier but I didn't because the question had been answered and a new one was being put and that was on the very same issue when my learned friend Mr. Rodic put to the witness, or said to the witness, this is on page 27, about halfway down the page, on this statement it says that you quote read it, meaning the statement. That is quite a misleading proposition and it is a misleading and incorrect statement, and that part of Mr. Rodic's cross-examination was put towards the -- put to the witness on a misleading basis. As Mr. Rodic well knows and has in his hand, the certificate of the interpreter which is on every -- every statement that the Prosecution takes, it's a standard form, and the one is the same, and the one on this particular statement says 2, this is by Andrea Bralic, the interpreter. Paragraph 2: "I have been informed by Mato Valjalo that he speaks and understands the Croatian language"; and 3, this is the important part, "I have orally translated the above statement from the English language to the Croatian language in the presence of Mato Valjalo who appeared to have heard and understood my translation of this statement." So when Mr. Rodic puts to the witness that he actually read the statement which, of course, was taken in English as all the statements are, it was misleading. So I object to that question and answer earlier and object to further line of questioning which is put on that basis. And I would ask Mr. Rodic to correct for the record the question he put to the witness before. And I further point out that in the statement what it actually says is in English: "During this time I was chauffeur for Zeljko Sikic, the head of the Territorial Defence for the Dubrovnik area." And the witness corrected it. It doesn't say "commander" in English. I haven't gone back to the Croatian to see whether it has been -- to see whether it said "commander" in Croatian, but the English, which was the one that was translated back to Mr. Valjalo at the time says "head", not "commander", and there's a difference. That's something I can go to in great length in re-direct -- or re-examination, but it's something which shouldn't be put to the witness in cross-examination. And in addition, the witness was never given a copy of the B/C/S until he actually got here, which has -- which unfortunately has been standard OTP practice, which was I think on last Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may. As for the first objection that the witness was -- read the statement from Croatian into English, this statement that he gave. I do fully accept my mistake, if indeed I've made one. I accept this objection from my colleague. However, I must point out that the difference in the Croatian language between the two expressions, "head" as it says allegedly in the English statement and "commander" as it would have read in the Croatian language, because originally it should read: "the commander of the TO", Territorial Defence. The Territorial Defence can only have a commander in the Croatia language. There are two different words being used for "commander" in Croatian and Serbian, but they both mean the same thing and refer to the same position. There's no such thing as head of the Territorial Defence. You can only have a commander of the Territorial Defence, but certainly no head. Therefore, Your Honour, I believe my time is up for my cross-examination, and I only have one further question to ask if I may. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Valjalo, we have agreed that you are 43 [as interpreted] years of age and that in 1991 you were an able-bodied man and that you had been given a war assignment. We have also agreed that you were on duty at the municipality between the 5th and the 6th of December, in the night between the 5th or 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was December. You did state this on various occasions.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have misspoken because you kept interrupting me, but it certainly wasn't the 5th and the 6th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The night between the 5th and the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's simply not correct. I was not on duty then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what you say now. But you did say several times, both in answer to my questions and questions of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant the first of October, because that was the only time I was on duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Valjalo, is it not correct that you do not have the first original document concerning your wounding?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. I don't have it on me right now, but I could easily obtain it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have agreed that you have the status of a -- of an invalid of war.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have agreed too, haven't we, that as a wound civilian, you ideally should not have been granted this status.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As a civilian -- as civilian, I would have been granted the status of a civilian invalid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Valjalo, I'm not challenging the fact that you were wounded. I'm challenging the location of your wounding, and I am putting it to you that you are a civilian casualty. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you actually -- you're not a civilian casualty?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do have papers showing that you are a military invalid of war?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We are agreed on that, but anything else concerning my wounding is beyond doubt, and all of it is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you. I have completed my cross-examination, and I apologise for spending a bit more time on it than originally planned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, you will, I'm sure, have noticed the validity of the objection by Mr. Re about the repetition of your questioning. There were a number of issues that you came back to, in some cases more than once. We have no need for that, and we can't afford the time for that in the course of this trial. Deal with an issue as you've done and then move on to another. Don't go back because you think it's a good point. We've heard it the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept the criticism, Your Honour, and I apologise for that. I will try not to repeat the same mistake in the future. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rodic. We will break now for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Re. Re-examined by Mr. Re:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Valjalo, Mr. Rodic asked you some questions about whether you saw any Croatian artillery pieces in Dubrovnik, and your response was you didn't see -- you said, "Not a single item, never in Dubrovnik." My question to you is when you were referring to Dubrovnik, were you referring to the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Old Town, yes, by all means, but I never saw any pieces of artillery in the general, broader town area either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also cross-examined about seeing warships in the harbour on the 1st of October, 1991, which you said were directly targeting the area. To which navy did those warships belong?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The warships belonged to the Yugoslav navy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Similarly you told Mr. Rodic that you saw planes targeting Srdj. To which air force did those planes belong?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also the Yugoslav air force. I saw them targeting Srdj. There were two aircraft.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the naval warships you saw at Lokrum, were they also of the Yugoslav navy or of another navy?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Yugoslav navy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Valjalo, you were questioned about seeing positions through your binoculars. You said that you could see things from various positions in the Old Town, and you also mentioned the Argentina Hotel and the Excelsior Hotel. Why did you go to the Argentina Hotel?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I went to the Argentina Hotel quite often. I drove some gentlemen there sometimes, the monitors, sometimes other personnel. Whenever I drove our people back home, I had to go around the Argentina Hotel because that area is full of one-way streets. The Argentina Hotel is where the monitors were staying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it that you went to the Argentine -- Argentina Hotel?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the day or the dates. I didn't keep a diary. But I did drive by the Argentina Hotel quite a number of times in a car. Whenever I was on my way to Lapad I had to go around the Argentina Hotel and pass by -- through Viktorija. It's a one-way street and every time you drive by, you pass by the Argentina Hotel on the way. You could see the positions from most parts of town. They were the nearest to the Argentina Hotel. I'm talking about the positions on Srdj or, rather, just below where the Croatian army positions were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your answer to me was you can't remember the day or the date. Was it between September 1991 and the 6th of December, 1991 when you were injured or was it some other time that you went to the Argentina Hotel?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went quite often, ever since the attack began in October. I would often drive by. That was the only road I could use to travel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My learned friend Mr. Rodic cross-examined you at some length on Friday about the fact that you did not produce, in May 2000, when interviewed by an OTP investigator, and didn't bring with you any records from the Dubrovnik hospital such as a letter of discharge. I want to show you three documents. Can you please put the first document, which is open, onto the overhead projector. Can you please have a look at it. Mr. Valjalo, can you please look at the document which is on the screen -- I'm sorry, the overhead projector there. Is that a letter from the medical centre in Dubrovnik dated the 12th of December, 1991, referring to your being wounded in Dubrovnik on the 6th of December, 1991, and being treated in the hospital at Dubrovnik from the 6th to the 12th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the letter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at the next document, which is a letter from the medical centre in Dubrovnik, which is undated. Is that one --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps I can be of assistance to my learned friend and colleague in connection with this document that we're looking at. In the lower corner -- my apologies, Your Honour. We just received these documents awhile ago, so we did not have sufficient time to familiarise ourselves with these documents. So my apologies. My remark does not relate to this document. I was mistaken about this. As for this document, what we can see clearly is that it's unsigned, and the last few lines are missing, so that's a problem that we seem to have with the document being displayed on the ELMO right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll see what the witness can say of the document. Thank you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution apologies to the Trial Chamber. We did not have these as yet translated into English. They were faxed to us on the weekend from Dubrovnik. And it appears that we only have one of a two-page document, but we'll do the best we can today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Valjalo, can you please read the first -- read aloud the first sentence of the document which you had on the screen and is there now.

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Wounded by an explosive device on the 6th of December, 1991, in the area of head and neck."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And is that --

utterances.speaker: MATO VALJALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The right," something, "thigh and lower leg." This document, I think, is from the Zagreb medical centre, because that's where another piece of shrapnel was found in my lung.
