And the paragraph is pointed out to him, then it's read out to him, and then suddenly he remembers. Your Honour, please if you could just bear this in mind. We don't think this is a proper way to ask questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you look at lines 20: "Are you familiar with this type of document?" "Yes, I have read it before, but I cannot give you all the details of what it -- of what is in it now, but yes, I've seen it before." Then I've asked him about the Old Town being shelled. He wasn't sure. Then I asked him to look at that line to refresh his recollection, and you see that on line 7, page 85. "Does that refresh your recollection? Answer: "Oh, yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave. My colleague has read everything out nicely, but he started at line 20 and omitted line 19 and so on and so forth. I wonder why he left that out, line 19, that's where the reading should have begun.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll go back and read it if you'd like. We can get the transcript right here, Judge. The -- I asked the witness to refresh his recollection, just like Mr. Rodic refreshed the witness's recollection earlier today. He read it out. I asked the witness to look at a document to see if that refreshes his recollection. It's an allowable technique in this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The witness has refreshed his recollection of what is in the document. It is his evidence, as I understand it, that he has no personal knowledge of the truth or otherwise of what he is recalling, but he is recalling what is written in the document. That, Mr. Petrovic is, as far as I understand the evidence on this point is presently going. Is there any concern you have about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my understanding is the same as yours. However, Your Honour, the road that my learned friend and colleague has taken to achieve this result ultimately had we not objected, the transcript would have been left to reflect the witness as having direct knowledge of all of this, as if this was something that issued directly from his testimony. There was an objection on our part which you have accepted, Your Honour. Now the situation is clear, but had it not been for our objection, we would have had the witness saying how the Old Town had been shelled and would have continued explaining that situation. We don't believe that's the proper road to take when examining a witness. Secondly, I am sure that my colleague is well able to distinguish between questions that should be asked on examination-in-chief and questions asked on cross-examination. I did not believe that an equation mark should have been drawn between these two different stages of proceedings. That's all I wished to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think Mr. Weiner is being careful to get it clearly from the witness that he has no personal knowledge of the actual facts behind the document, and I at least am hearing his evidence about this aspect on that basis. So, Mr. Weiner, if you'd like to carry on for a few brief moments it's going to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you please turn to paragraph 5, which is on page 2 of the document. I'd like to read the second and third sentences to you to try and move this along. "Dubrovnik itself has no military or strategic value, although it is of considerable economic importance to the region, being perhaps the greatest tourist attraction in Yugoslavia. The fact that the JNA have shelled the Old City indicates their lack of concern for the economic consequences of their actions." Sir, do you agree with that statement?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And please explain why.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF
utterances.text: Well, to me as a person, whatever is said is correct. I cannot see that Dubrovnik had any military value. I considered Dubrovnik to be of great importance for the area, economically and as a tourist attraction. I saw no reason personally for using Dubrovnik as a target for any military action and certainly not for shelling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Is it time to break now, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It seems to be, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Hvalkof, I must ask you to return again tomorrow to continue your evidence. If you'd be so good as to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will adjourn now for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
